stem: Vanadium is a transition element in Period 4 of the Periodic Table.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Vanadium shows typical chemical properties of transition elements, including variable oxidation states.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State **two** other typical chemical properties of transition elements.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why transition elements have variable oxidation states.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
$\text{VO}_2^+$ can be reduced to $\text{V}^{2+}$ by $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ in acidic conditions.

equation 2 $$2\text{VO}_2^+ + 3\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + 8\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{V}^{2+} + 6\text{CO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
In a titration, $25.00\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.0300\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{VO}_2^+(\text{aq})$ is added to $10\text{ cm}^3$ of dilute sulfuric acid.

A solution of $0.0400\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}(\text{aq})$ is then added from a burette until the end-point is reached.

The titration is repeated and concordant results obtained, as shown in Table 3.1.

Table 3.1

|  | 1 | 2 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| volume of $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}(\text{aq})$ added/$\text{cm}^3$ | 28.15 | 28.10 |

Show that these results are consistent with the stoichiometry of equation 2.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
An excess of $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ reacts with $\text{VO}_2^+$ to form a mixture of two octahedral complex ions. The complex ions are stereoisomers of each other.

Each complex ion contains a $\text{V}^{2+}$ cation and three $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ ions.

Complete the diagram to show the three-dimensional structure of **one** of the complex ions.

Include the charge of the complex ion.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Use O O to represent a $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ ion.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
$\text{V}^{2+}(\text{aq})$ can be oxidised by $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2(\text{aq})$.

Table 3.2 gives some relevant data.

Table 3.2

|  | half-equation | $E^\ominus / \text{V}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2(\text{aq}) + 2\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$ | +1.77 |
| 2 | $\text{VO}_2^+(\text{aq}) + 2\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{VO}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$ | +1.00 |
| 3 | $\text{VO}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{V}^{3+}(\text{aq}) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$ | +0.34 |
| 4 | $\text{V}^{3+}(\text{aq}) + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{V}^{2+}(\text{aq})$ | -0.26 |

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
Identify the vanadium species that forms when an excess of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2(\text{aq})$ reacts with $\text{V}^{2+}(\text{aq})$ under standard conditions.

Explain your answer with reference to the data in Table 3.2.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Concentrated acidified $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ can react with $\text{V}^{2+}$ to form red $\text{VO}_2^{3+}$ ions.

$\text{VO}_2^{3+}$ contains vanadium combined with the peroxide anion, $\text{O}_2^{2-}$.

Deduce the oxidation state of vanadium in $\text{VO}_2^{3+}$.
